**Finding: Deviation** — no express performance warranty from HDI.

**What I found**

Section 9 ("Warranties") is the only warranty provision in the Agreement, and it does no warranty work at all:
- **9(a)** (p0056–p0057) — mutual corporate-authority reps only: organization, power, enforceability, no conflict.
- **9(b)** (p0058) — merely an acknowledgment about the pre-existing Globix hosting agreement, which actually benefits us.

Nothing in the document warrants that HDI's design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance, management or hosting of the Site will meet any standard, conform to any specification, comply with law, or be free of malicious code — and there is no remedy. Searches for "workmanlike", "industry standard", "MERCHANTABILITY" and "AS IS" all returned nothing. Sections 1 and 5 impose only bare performance obligations (e.g., 1.6's 60/70-day operational deadline), not warranties.

**Why it's a deviation, not walk-away or compliant**

The good news: there is no disclaimer, so this isn't "AS IS" walk-away territory. But the fallback still requires an express performance warranty with a real remedy (90 days software / 30 days services). Zero warranty and zero remedy fails the fallback on a material term, and the detection guidance expressly directs that a missing express warranty be inserted as a deviation. This is a gap running against HDI, so it is properly flagged.

**The redline** (validated `ok:true`)

New Section 9(c) at the preferred position: workmanlike Services consistent with industry standards; 90-day conformance period; compliance with law; no malicious code — with re-performance or repair/replacement at HDI's option, backstopped by a refund of fees paid if HDI fails to cure within thirty days.

Two drafting points worth noting:
- I tied the 90-day conformance period to the Company's **written acceptance under Section 5.2** rather than a generic "delivery," since 5.2 gives us exclusive acceptance rights and no part of the Site goes live without our written approval. That makes the clock start at a date we control.
- Because "Services" is used in Section 8.1 but never defined, I defined it in the inserted text by reference to the Section 1.1/1.2 scope, which cures a latent gap.
- **Section 10.7 already lists Section 9 as surviving for two years**, so the new warranty inherits survival with no further edits needed.

The comment offers the 30-day services fallback as a negotiating concession.
